newsitem.title: PANAMA: PANAMA HOSTS ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING CONGRESS.
newsitem.headline: PANAMA HOSTS ANTI-MONEY LAUNDERING CONGRESS.

text.p: Government agencies hunting for dirty money met with international bankers in Panama on Wednesday for a three-day congress on the prevention of money laundering.

The conference will debate means to improve cooperation between governments, banks, brokerage firms and agencies trying to stop money laundering. It will also focus on how to spot laundering in the stock market and in international trade.

"We know we can't stop it (money laundering) right away, but this conference is a good step towards combating it," Charles Klingman of the U.S. Treasury's Financial Crimes Enforcement Network (FINCEN) told Reuters.

Participants at the congress, sponsored by FINCEN, the Organization of American States and the Panamanian Banking Association, will also discuss how to develop customer profiles and spot suspicious transactions.
But one delegate from the Caribbean island of Aruba remained sceptical. "We've already lost the battle against money laundering. Now we're just trying to stay afloat", he said.
A U.S. banker, who asked not to be named, added: "When it comes to money laundering conferences there's a lot of talk but little action afterwards."
Over 400 delegates from over 18 countries are attending the conference, including U.S. and Latin American bankers and members of the international police organization Interpol.
(( -- Paul de Bendern, Panama City newsroom, 507-223 7739))
